governanceNotes: D1 batch 48 (2026-09-24): deferred. Manifestation-identity screen recorded 2026-09-24: (i) the catalogue identity is a site-specific denervating finding rather than a disease, and the located literature documents it as a sign of an upstream nerve lesion - a QJM clinical-image record of interosseous muscle atrophy, an ultrasound and nerve-transfer literature in which the finding is measured as an outcome of ulnar and median nerve injury, and mid-palm ganglion-cyst and neuralgic-amyotrophy series in which the atrophy follows the nerve lesion - so the causal arrows run inward from those primaries and an outgoing edge would invert the direction of the located evidence (direction-inversion and entity-mismatch guards); (ii) the only catalog-fit outward target is the muscle-atrophy umbrella, which this identity instantiates, and mirroring the existing guyon-s-canal-syndrome-to-muscle-atrophy direct-causation edge from the atrophy side would restate that relationship from the wrong end (constitutive/umbrella and direction guards); (iii) no condition-specific evidence quantifying a downstream catalogue outcome (loss-of-use-of-extremities, unexplained-chronic-pain, contractures, or a hand-function measure) in patients identified by interosseous atrophy was located, so any outgoing edge would rest on nerve-lesion populations rather than on this identity (zero-record guard); (iv) the sibling finding identity thenar-hypotenar-atrophy is queued under the same manifest-identity treatment so the two hand-atrophy findings are handled consistently. Reopening condition: a cohort or series in which interosseous atrophy is the documented index finding with a catalog-fit secondary outcome, or a governance decision that folds this identity into the nerve-lesion identities that produce it.
